defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard do
  @moduledoc """
  The account's configurable rates, one per pricing model.

  A single row per account (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card/1`).
  A rate left blank means that pricing model isn't priced yet — quoting
  against it is refused until the owner sets a rate (see
  `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`).

  `weekly_discount_percent`/`biweekly_discount_percent`/`monthly_discount_percent`
  and `add_on_rates_cents` exist for the public instant-quote calculator
  (story 848, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`) — a recurring frequency's
  discount off the one-time subtotal, and the configured price for each
  named add-on (e.g. `"inside_fridge" => 1500`). Unset (`nil`) means no
  discount; an add-on key missing from the map means it isn't priced
  yet, same "never guess a price" rule as the base rates.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          per_sqft_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          weekly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          biweekly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          monthly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          add_on_rates_cents: %{optional(String.t()) => integer()},
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "rate_cards" do
    field :per_room_bedroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_room_bathroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_sqft_rate_cents, :integer
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :weekly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :biweekly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :monthly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :add_on_rates_cents, :map, default: %{}

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @rate_fields ~w(per_room_bedroom_rate_cents per_room_bathroom_rate_cents
                  per_sqft_rate_cents hourly_rate_cents weekly_discount_percent
                  biweekly_discount_percent monthly_discount_percent add_on_rates_cents)a

  @discount_fields ~w(weekly_discount_percent biweekly_discount_percent monthly_discount_percent)a

  def changeset(rate_card, attrs) do
    rate_card
    |> cast(attrs, @rate_fields)
    |> validate_number(:per_room_bedroom_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:per_room_bathroom_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:per_sqft_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:hourly_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_discount_percents()
    |> validate_add_on_rates()
  end

  defp validate_discount_percents(changeset) do
    Enum.reduce(@discount_fields, changeset, fn field, changeset ->
      changeset
      |> validate_number(field, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
      |> validate_number(field, less_than_or_equal_to: 100)
    end)
  end

  # Every configured amount must be a non-negative integer number of
  # cents — the same shape every other rate on this card takes.
  defp validate_add_on_rates(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :add_on_rates_cents) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      rates ->
        if Enum.all?(rates, fn {key, cents} -> is_binary(key) and valid_cents?(cents) end) do
          changeset
        else
          add_error(changeset, :add_on_rates_cents, "must map add-on names to whole cent amounts")
        end
    end
  end

  defp valid_cents?(cents), do: is_integer(cents) and cents >= 0
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Quotes built from the account's rate card using per-room, per-sqft,
4	  or hourly pricing models.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. A quote is
7	  built up in memory (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`) and only ever
8	  persisted at the moment it's sent — `send_quote/3` freezes the rate
9	  card's current rates into the quote's line items, so later rate-card
10	  edits never alter an already-sent quote.
11	  """
12	
13	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
14	
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
17	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
18	  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, QuoteItem, RateCard, Pricing}
19	
20	  ## Rate card
21	
22	  @doc """
23	  Returns the account's rate card, creating a blank one on first use.
24	  """
25	  def get_or_create_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
26	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
27	    case Repo.get_by(RateCard, account_id: account_id) do
28	      nil -> Repo.insert!(%RateCard{account_id: account_id})
29	      rate_card -> rate_card
30	    end
31	  end
32	
33	  def change_rate_card(%Scope{}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs \\ %{}) do
34	    RateCard.changeset(rate_card, attrs)
35	  end
36	
37	  def update_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs)
38	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
39	    rate_card
40	    |> RateCard.changeset(attrs)
41	    |> Repo.update()
42	  end
43	
44	  ## Quotes
45	
46	  def change_quote(%Scope{}, %Quote{} = quote, attrs \\ %{}) do
47	    Quote.changeset(quote, attrs)
48	  end
49	
50	  @doc """
51	  Lists the account's quotes, most recently sent first.
52	  """
53	  def list_quotes(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
54	    Quote
55	    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
56	    |> order_by([q], desc: q.inserted_at)
57	    |> Repo.all()
58	  end
59	
60	  def get_quote!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
61	    Quote
62	    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
63	    |> preload(:quote_items)
64	    |> Repo.get!(id)
65	  end
66

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting do
  @moduledoc """
  Quotes built from the account's rate card using per-room, per-sqft,
  or hourly pricing models.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. A quote is
  built up in memory (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`) and only ever
  persisted at the moment it's sent — `send_quote/3` freezes the rate
  card's current rates into the quote's line items, so later rate-card
  edits never alter an already-sent quote.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, QuoteItem, RateCard, Pricing}

  ## Rate card

  @doc """
  Returns the account's rate card, creating a blank one on first use.
  """
  def get_or_create_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(RateCard, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> Repo.insert!(%RateCard{account_id: account_id})
      rate_card -> rate_card
    end
  end

  def change_rate_card(%Scope{}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RateCard.changeset(rate_card, attrs)
  end

  def update_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    rate_card
    |> RateCard.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Quotes

  def change_quote(%Scope{}, %Quote{} = quote, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Quote.changeset(quote, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists the account's quotes, most recently sent first.
  """
  def list_quotes(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Quote
    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([q], desc: q.inserted_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_quote!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Quote
    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(:quote_items)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Finalizes a draft quote against the current rate card: prices every
  line item, then inserts the quote and its `CleanerCrm.Quoting.QuoteItem`s
  together, freezing the rates and amounts at this moment.

  Refuses with `{:error, :not_finalizable}` when any priced line item
  is missing a rate on the rate card, or the total isn't positive — a
  sent quote can never be a zero-dollar or partially-rated quote.
  """
  def send_quote(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Quote{} = draft,
        %RateCard{} = rate_card
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    line_items = Pricing.line_items(rate_card, draft)

    if Pricing.finalizable?(line_items) do
      insert_sent_quote(scope, account_id, draft, line_items)
    else
      {:error, :not_finalizable}
    end
  end

  defp insert_sent_quote(scope, account_id, draft, line_items) do
    quote_attrs = %{
      client_id: draft.client_id,
      client_name: draft.client_name,
      client_phone: draft.client_phone,
      pricing_model: draft.pricing_model,
      bedroom_count: draft.bedroom_count,
      bathroom_count: draft.bathroom_count,
      square_feet: draft.square_feet,
      hours: draft.hours,
      status: :sent,
      total_cents: Pricing.total_cents(line_items),
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    }

    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      with {:ok, quote} <-
             %Quote{account_id: account_id} |> Quote.changeset(quote_attrs) |> Repo.insert(),
           {:ok, _items} <- insert_quote_items(quote, line_items) do
        Recorder.record(scope, "quote_sent", "Quote", quote.id, %{}, %{
          "total_cents" => quote.total_cents
        })

        quote
      else
        {:error, changeset} -> Repo.rollback(changeset)
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_quote_items(quote, line_items) do
    Enum.reduce_while(line_items, {:ok, []}, fn line_item, {:ok, acc} ->
      case %QuoteItem{quote_id: quote.id} |> QuoteItem.changeset(line_item) |> Repo.insert() do
        {:ok, quote_item} -> {:cont, {:ok, [quote_item | acc]}}
        {:error, _changeset} = error -> {:halt, error}
      end
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing do
  @moduledoc """
  Computes a quote's line items and total from a rate card, and decides
  whether a quote is ready to send.

  Pure and side-effect free: it never touches the database, so
  `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.Builder` can call it on every keystroke for
  live totals, and `CleanerCrm.Quoting.send_quote/3` can call it again
  at the moment of persistence.

  Per the money-handling ADR, rate math is done in `Decimal` and
  rounded half-up to whole cents.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, RateCard}

  @type line_item :: %{
          description: String.t(),
          quantity: integer(),
          rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer()
        }

  @doc """
  The quote form field names (as submitted param keys) that belong to
  a given pricing model — used to drop inputs left over from a
  previously selected model when the owner switches models.
  """
  @spec fields_for_model(String.t()) :: [String.t()]
  def fields_for_model("per_room"), do: ~w(bedroom_count bathroom_count)
  def fields_for_model("per_sqft"), do: ~w(square_feet)
  def fields_for_model("hourly"), do: ~w(hours)
  def fields_for_model(_other), do: []

  @doc """
  The priced line items for a quote's chosen model. Only items with a
  positive quantity are included — an empty or zero field never
  demands a rate. A `nil` `rate_cents` means the rate card has nothing
  configured yet for that item, and its amount is zero.
  """
  @spec line_items(RateCard.t(), Quote.t()) :: [line_item()]
  def line_items(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Quote{} = quote) do
    quote.pricing_model
    |> model_items(rate_card, quote)
    |> Enum.filter(&(&1.quantity > 0))
  end

  defp model_items(:per_room, rate_card, quote) do
    [
      item("Bedrooms", quote.bedroom_count, rate_card.per_room_bedroom_rate_cents),
      item("Bathrooms", quote.bathroom_count, rate_card.per_room_bathroom_rate_cents)
    ]
  end

  defp model_items(:per_sqft, rate_card, quote) do
    [item("Square footage", quote.square_feet, rate_card.per_sqft_rate_cents)]
  end

  defp model_items(:hourly, rate_card, quote) do
    [item("Hours", quote.hours, rate_card.hourly_rate_cents)]
  end

  defp model_items(nil, _rate_card, _quote), do: []

  defp item(description, quantity, rate_cents) do
    quantity = quantity || 0

    %{
      description: description,
      quantity: quantity,
      rate_cents: rate_cents,
      amount_cents: amount_cents(quantity, rate_cents)
    }
  end

  defp amount_cents(quantity, rate_cents)
       when is_integer(quantity) and is_integer(rate_cents) and quantity > 0 do
    quantity
    |> Decimal.new()
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.new(rate_cents))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end

  defp amount_cents(_quantity, _rate_cents), do: 0

  @doc "Sums a quote's line items into its total, in cents."
  @spec total_cents([line_item()]) :: integer()
  def total_cents(line_items), do: Enum.reduce(line_items, 0, &(&1.amount_cents + &2))

  @doc "Whether any priced line item is missing a rate from the rate card."
  @spec missing_rate?([line_item()]) :: boolean()
  def missing_rate?(line_items), do: Enum.any?(line_items, &is_nil(&1.rate_cents))

  @doc """
  Whether a quote is ready to send: at least one priced line item,
  every one of them rated, and a positive total.
  """
  @spec finalizable?([line_item()]) :: boolean()
  def finalizable?(line_items) do
    line_items != [] and not missing_rate?(line_items) and total_cents(line_items) > 0
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index

## Phoenix 1.8 Form Component Pattern

**Structure**: Create a single LiveView module handling both `:new` and `:edit` actions with these required elements:

1. **Module Setup**
   ```elixir
   defmodule AppWeb.ResourceLive.Form do
     use AppWeb, :live_view
     alias App.Context
     alias App.Context.Schema
   ```

2. **Required Functions**
   - `render/1` - Form template with `phx-change="validate"` and `phx-submit="save"`
   - `mount/3` - Extract `return_to` param and call `apply_action/3`
   - `apply_action/3` - Pattern match on `:new`/`:edit`, set page title, schema, and form
   - `handle_event/3` - Handle "validate" and "save" events
   - `save_resource/3` - Pattern match on action, call context create/update functions

3. **Key Patterns**
   - Use `to_form(changeset)` for form assignment
   - Handle validation with `action: :validate` on changeset errors
   - Navigate on success with `push_navigate/2`
   - Support `return_to` parameter for flexible navigation
   - Use consistent flash messages: "Resource created/updated successfully"

4. **Template Requirements**
   - Wrap in layout component with flash and current_scope
   - Include header with dynamic page title
   - Form with proper field inputs and submit/cancel buttons
   - Cancel button navigates to computed return path

This pattern ensures consistent CRUD form behavior across your Phoenix 1.8 application.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Money do
  @moduledoc """
  Formats integer cents for display, per the money-handling ADR: every
  amount is stored and computed as integer cents, and this is the only
  place a dollar string gets built.
  """

  @doc """
  Formats integer cents as `"$X.XX"`, with thousands separators. `nil`
  is treated as zero.

  ## Examples

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(18_000)
      "$180.00"

      iex> CleanerCrm.Money.format_cents(nil)
      "$0.00"
  """
  @spec format_cents(integer() | nil) :: String.t()
  def format_cents(nil), do: format_cents(0)

  def format_cents(cents) when is_integer(cents) do
    sign = if cents < 0, do: "-", else: ""
    dollars = div(abs(cents), 100)
    remainder = rem(abs(cents), 100)

    "#{sign}$#{group_thousands(dollars)}.#{pad_cents(remainder)}"
  end

  defp pad_cents(remainder), do: remainder |> Integer.to_string() |> String.pad_leading(2, "0")

  defp group_thousands(dollars) do
    dollars
    |> Integer.to_string()
    |> String.reverse()
    |> String.replace(~r/(\d{3})(?=\d)/, "\\1,")
    |> String.reverse()
  end
end

defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id})

  defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id})

  defp pay_type_options, do: [{"Hourly", "hourly"}, {"Piece rate", "piece_rate"}]

  defp pay_type_value(form) do
    case form[:pay_type].value do
      nil -> ""
      value -> to_string(value)
    end
  end

  # `hourly_rate`/`piece_rate` aren't real `Job` fields (only the
  # `_cents` columns are), so there's nothing on the changeset to
  # source a freshly-loaded job's dollar display from — this mirrors
  # `with_display_price/1` above, computed straight off whichever
  # `_cents` field matches the job's `pay_type`.
  defp initial_pay_rate_input(%Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: cents})
       when is_integer(cents),
       do: cents_to_dollars(cents)

  defp initial_pay_rate_input(%Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: cents})
       when is_integer(cents),
       do: cents_to_dollars(cents)

  defp initial_pay_rate_input(%Job{}), do: ""

  defp cents_to_dollars(cents),
    do: cents |> Decimal.new() |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100)) |> Decimal.to_string(:normal)

  # Pulls the submitted dollar rate back out for redisplay (there's no
  # changeset field to read it from, per `initial_pay_rate_input/1`
  # above) and rewrites the matching `job[params]` key to
  # `*_rate_cents` before the changeset ever sees it — clearing the
  # other pay type's rate so switching pay types doesn't leave a
  # stale, unused rate behind.
  defp split_pay_params(%{"pay_type" => "hourly", "hourly_rate" => dollars} = params) do
    {dollars,
     params
     |> Map.put("hourly_rate_cents", dollars_to_cents(dollars))
     |> Map.put("piece_rate_cents", nil)}
  end

  defp split_pay_params(%{"pay_type" => "piece_rate", "piece_rate" => dollars} = params) do
    {dollars,
     params
     |> Map.put("piece_rate_cents", dollars_to_cents(dollars))
     |> Map.put("hourly_rate_cents", nil)}
  end

  defp split_pay_params(%{"pay_type" => ""} = params) do
    {"", params |> Map.put("hourly_rate_cents", nil) |> Map.put("piece_rate_cents", nil)}
  end

  defp split_pay_params(params), do: {"", params}

  # An unparseable dollar amount (or a blank input) becomes `nil`
  # rather than a changeset error — the rate is optional at the schema
  # level, same as `agreed_price`, so an invalid entry is treated as
  # "not set yet" rather than blocking the rest of the form.
  defp dollars_to_cents(dollars) when is_binary(dollars) do
    case Decimal.parse(String.trim(dollars)) do
      {decimal, ""} ->
        decimal |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()

      _ ->
        nil
    end
  end

  defp dollars_to_cents(_dollars), do: nil

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Public acquisition funnel (stories 848/849): the instant-quote
4	  calculator, capturing a lead's contact info once a price is shown,
5	  and quote acceptance — slot selection, cancellation-policy
6	  agreement, and Stripe card capture — that converts an accepted lead
7	  into a client + property + plan/job and issues portal access.
8	
9	  Orchestrates `CleanerCrm.Quoting` (rate-card pricing, via
10	  `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`), `CleanerCrm.Clients` (client +
11	  property), `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` (job/plan + slot availability),
12	  `CleanerCrm.Billing` (card capture via its `StripeGateway`), and
13	  `CleanerCrm.Portal` (the confirmation's magic-link).
14	
15	  Every function here is either scoped by an explicit `Scope`
16	  (mirroring every other context) or takes a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead`
17	  directly and resolves its own account scope from it — none of them
18	  are reachable from a logged-in user, so there's no caller `Scope` to
19	  receive from a plug.
20	
21	  ## Single-tenant storefront (known MVP limitation)
22	
23	  `/book` carries no account identifier — no slug, no subdomain — so
24	  `public_scope/0` resolves to the *most recently created* account
25	  rather than *the right* one, matching the single-account assumption
26	  every story-848 spec drives (each spec's own account is the newest
27	  one the moment it hits `/book`, so this holds even alongside stray
28	  older rows). A multi-tenant deployment needs its own story to give
29	  each business a distinct public booking URL (e.g. `/book/:slug`)
30	  before this holds up outside a single-account deployment or test.
31	  """
32	
33	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
34	
35	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account
36	  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway
37	  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.{Lead, Notifier, Pricing}
38	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
39	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
40	  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
41	  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
42	  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard
43	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
44	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
45	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
46	
47	  # A reasonable number of visits to materialize up front for a
48	  # recurring booking, matching the office's own recurring-plan
49	  # builder default order of magnitude (see
50	  # `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent`) — the office can
51	  # always add more from the schedule board afterward.
52	  @default_occurrence_count 12
53	  @default_visit_duration_seconds 2 * 60 * 60
54	
55	  ## Public storefront
56	
57	  @doc "The (single-account MVP) scope every unauthenticated booking-funnel call resolves against."
58	  def public_scope, do: %Scope{active_account_id: resolve_public_account_id()}
59	
60	  @doc "The public rate card the instant-quote calculator prices against."
61	  def get_rate_card(%Scope{} = scope), do: Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)
62	
63	  defp resolve_public_account_id do
64	    Account
65	    |> order_by(desc: :inserted_at)
66	    |> limit(1)
67	    |> select([a], a.id)
68	    |> Repo.one()
69	  end
70	
71	  ## Instant quote (calculator)
72	
73	  @doc """
74	  The calculator's live-preview changeset — never persisted, so the
75	  price can be computed before any contact info exists (see
76	  `quote_summary/2`).
77	  """
78	  def change_lead(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.quote_changeset(lead, attrs)
79	
80	  @doc "Everything `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` needs to render the live total."
81	  def quote_summary(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead),
82	    do: Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)
83	
84	  @doc """
85	  Captures a visitor's contact info against their computed price —
86	  locking in the quote as an accepted lead with its own acceptance
87	  token, the moment `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote`'s contact form is
88	  submitted. Always saved as `:accepted`: a lead is only ever persisted
89	  once contact info makes it one.
90	  """
91	  def create_lead(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
92	    %Lead{account_id: account_id}
93	    |> Lead.changeset(Map.merge(attrs, %{acceptance_token: generate_token(), status: :accepted}))
94	    |> Repo.insert()
95	  end
96	
97	  @doc "Looks up an accepted lead by its public acceptance-link token. No `Scope` — the token is the access control."
98	  def get_lead_by_token(token) when is_binary(token),
99	    do: Repo.get_by(Lead, acceptance_token: token)
100	
101	  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)
102	
103	  ## Acceptance: slot selection
104	
105	  def change_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.slot_changeset(lead, attrs)
106	
107	  @doc """
108	  Validates and applies a slot choice to the (still unpersisted) lead.
109	  Nothing reaches the database here — `confirm_booking/2` is the only
110	  place a slot gets written, so availability is always checked again
111	  right before a card is ever charged, no matter how long a client
112	  lingers on the cancellation-policy step.
113	  """
114	  def select_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs) do
115	    with {:ok, %Lead{start_time: start_time} = slotted} <-
116	           lead |> Lead.slot_changeset(attrs) |> Ecto.Changeset.apply_action(:update) do
117	      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
118	    end
119	  end
120	
121	  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
122	    candidate = Time.add(start_time, @default_visit_duration_seconds, :second)
123	    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
124	  end
125	
126	  ## Acceptance: cancellation policy + payment
127	
128	  def change_confirmation(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}),
129	    do: Lead.confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs)
130	
131	  @doc "Whether the lead's selected slot is still free, account-wide (single-crew capacity, not per-cleaner)."
132	  def slot_available?(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: false
133	
134	  def slot_available?(%Lead{} = lead) do
135	    Scheduling.slot_available?(
136	      scope_for(lead),
137	      lead.scheduled_date,
138	      lead.start_time,
139	      lead.end_time
140	    )
141	  end
142	
143	  @doc """
144	  The confirmation step. Refuses without charging anything when the
145	  cancellation policy isn't agreed to, or the slot's been claimed by
146	  another booking since it was selected — otherwise submits the card
147	  and moves the lead to `:payment_pending`. Only the Stripe webhook
148	  (`receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever confirms or declines it from
149	  there, per the same webhook-confirms-everything rule
150	  `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for invoice payments.
151	  """
152	  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, %{"payment_method" => payment_method} = params) do
153	    cond do
154	      Map.get(params, "policy_agreed") not in [true, "true"] ->
155	        {:error, :policy_required}
156	
157	      not slot_available?(lead) ->
158	        {:error, :slot_unavailable}
159	
160	      true ->
161	        submit_payment(lead, payment_method)
162	    end
163	  end
164	
165	  defp submit_payment(%Lead{} = lead, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
166	    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
167	           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
168	             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
169	             payment_method: payment_method,
170	             off_session: false,
171	             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
172	           }) do
173	      lead
174	      |> Lead.changeset(%{
175	        policy_agreed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
176	        status: :payment_pending,
177	        stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id
178	      })
179	      # `select_slot/2` never touches the database (see its doc) — the
180	      # slot lives only on this in-memory `lead` struct until now, so
181	      # `cast/3` (which diffs against the struct's own field, not the
182	      # row) would otherwise see "no change" and silently leave the
183	      # database's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time at `nil`.
184	      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:scheduled_date, lead.scheduled_date)
185	      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:start_time, lead.start_time)
186	      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:end_time, lead.end_time)
187	      |> Repo.update()
188	    end
189	  end
190	
191	  ## Webhook
192	
193	  @doc """
194	  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request for a
195	  booking's payment — `CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController` falls
196	  back to this once `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1` reports the
197	  event isn't one of its own invoices.
198	  """
199	  def receive_payment_webhook(conn) do
200	    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
201	      apply_webhook_event(event)
202	    end
203	  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking do
  @moduledoc """
  Public acquisition funnel (stories 848/849): the instant-quote
  calculator, capturing a lead's contact info once a price is shown,
  and quote acceptance — slot selection, cancellation-policy
  agreement, and Stripe card capture — that converts an accepted lead
  into a client + property + plan/job and issues portal access.

  Orchestrates `CleanerCrm.Quoting` (rate-card pricing, via
  `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`), `CleanerCrm.Clients` (client +
  property), `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` (job/plan + slot availability),
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` (card capture via its `StripeGateway`), and
  `CleanerCrm.Portal` (the confirmation's magic-link).

  Every function here is either scoped by an explicit `Scope`
  (mirroring every other context) or takes a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead`
  directly and resolves its own account scope from it — none of them
  are reachable from a logged-in user, so there's no caller `Scope` to
  receive from a plug.

  ## Single-tenant storefront (known MVP limitation)

  `/book` carries no account identifier — no slug, no subdomain — so
  `public_scope/0` resolves to the *most recently created* account
  rather than *the right* one, matching the single-account assumption
  every story-848 spec drives (each spec's own account is the newest
  one the moment it hits `/book`, so this holds even alongside stray
  older rows). A multi-tenant deployment needs its own story to give
  each business a distinct public booking URL (e.g. `/book/:slug`)
  before this holds up outside a single-account deployment or test.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.{Lead, Notifier, Pricing}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # A reasonable number of visits to materialize up front for a
  # recurring booking, matching the office's own recurring-plan
  # builder default order of magnitude (see
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent`) — the office can
  # always add more from the schedule board afterward.
  @default_occurrence_count 12
  @default_visit_duration_seconds 2 * 60 * 60

  ## Public storefront

  @doc "The (single-account MVP) scope every unauthenticated booking-funnel call resolves against."
  def public_scope, do: %Scope{active_account_id: resolve_public_account_id()}

  @doc "The public rate card the instant-quote calculator prices against."
  def get_rate_card(%Scope{} = scope), do: Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)

  defp resolve_public_account_id do
    Account
    |> order_by(desc: :inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([a], a.id)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Instant quote (calculator)

  @doc """
  The calculator's live-preview changeset — never persisted, so the
  price can be computed before any contact info exists (see
  `quote_summary/2`).
  """
  def change_lead(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.quote_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc "Everything `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` needs to render the live total."
  def quote_summary(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead),
    do: Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)

  @doc """
  Captures a visitor's contact info against their computed price —
  locking in the quote as an accepted lead with its own acceptance
  token, the moment `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote`'s contact form is
  submitted. Always saved as `:accepted`: a lead is only ever persisted
  once contact info makes it one.
  """
  def create_lead(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Lead{account_id: account_id}
    |> Lead.changeset(Map.merge(attrs, %{acceptance_token: generate_token(), status: :accepted}))
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "Looks up an accepted lead by its public acceptance-link token. No `Scope` — the token is the access control."
  def get_lead_by_token(token) when is_binary(token),
    do: Repo.get_by(Lead, acceptance_token: token)

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  ## Acceptance: slot selection

  def change_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.slot_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc """
  Validates and applies a slot choice to the (still unpersisted) lead.
  Nothing reaches the database here — `confirm_booking/2` is the only
  place a slot gets written, so availability is always checked again
  right before a card is ever charged, no matter how long a client
  lingers on the cancellation-policy step.
  """
  def select_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs) do
    with {:ok, %Lead{start_time: start_time} = slotted} <-
           lead |> Lead.slot_changeset(attrs) |> Ecto.Changeset.apply_action(:update) do
      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
    end
  end

  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, @default_visit_duration_seconds, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  ## Acceptance: cancellation policy + payment

  def change_confirmation(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}),
    do: Lead.confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc "Whether the lead's selected slot is still free, account-wide (single-crew capacity, not per-cleaner)."
  def slot_available?(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: false

  def slot_available?(%Lead{} = lead) do
    Scheduling.slot_available?(
      scope_for(lead),
      lead.scheduled_date,
      lead.start_time,
      lead.end_time
    )
  end

  @doc """
  The confirmation step. Refuses without charging anything when the
  cancellation policy isn't agreed to, or the slot's been claimed by
  another booking since it was selected — otherwise submits the card
  and moves the lead to `:payment_pending`. Only the Stripe webhook
  (`receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever confirms or declines it from
  there, per the same webhook-confirms-everything rule
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for invoice payments.
  """
  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, %{"payment_method" => payment_method} = params) do
    cond do
      Map.get(params, "policy_agreed") not in [true, "true"] ->
        {:error, :policy_required}

      not slot_available?(lead) ->
        {:error, :slot_unavailable}

      true ->
        submit_payment(lead, payment_method)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(%Lead{} = lead, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
             payment_method: payment_method,
             off_session: false,
             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
           }) do
      lead
      |> Lead.changeset(%{
        policy_agreed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
        status: :payment_pending,
        stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id
      })
      # `select_slot/2` never touches the database (see its doc) — the
      # slot lives only on this in-memory `lead` struct until now, so
      # `cast/3` (which diffs against the struct's own field, not the
      # row) would otherwise see "no change" and silently leave the
      # database's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time at `nil`.
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:scheduled_date, lead.scheduled_date)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:start_time, lead.start_time)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:end_time, lead.end_time)
      |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request for a
  booking's payment — `CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController` falls
  back to this once `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1` reports the
  event isn't one of its own invoices.
  """
  def receive_payment_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      convert_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      decline_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:error, :lead_not_found}

  defp find_lead_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"lead_id" => lead_id}} when is_binary(lead_id) -> fetch_lead(lead_id)
      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) -> fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id)
      _ -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead(lead_id) do
    case Repo.get(Lead, lead_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Lead, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp decline_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    lead |> Lead.changeset(%{status: :payment_declined}) |> Repo.update()
  end

  # Idempotent against a redelivered webhook — Stripe (and its Test
  # stand-in) offers no stronger delivery guarantee than at-least-once.
  defp convert_lead(%Lead{status: :converted} = lead), do: {:ok, lead}

  defp convert_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    scope = scope_for(lead)

    with {:ok, {updated, client}} <-
           Repo.transact(fn ->
             with {:ok, client} <- Clients.create_client(scope, client_attrs(lead)),
                  {:ok, property} <- Clients.create_property(scope, property_attrs(client)),
                  {:ok, visit_ids} <- schedule_visit(scope, lead, property),
                  {:ok, updated} <- finalize_conversion(lead, client, property, visit_ids) do
               {:ok, {updated, client}}
             end
           end) do
      issue_portal_access(updated, client)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp client_attrs(%Lead{} = lead) do
    %{
      name: lead.client_name,
      email: lead.client_email,
      phone: lead.client_phone,
      card_on_file: true
    }
  end

  # No property inputs exist anywhere in the public funnel (story 848's
  # form only ever asks for what prices the job) — the office fills
  # the real address in from the client record afterward. Named after
  # the client rather than a generic placeholder so the schedule board
  # (which shows a job's property, never its client, on the card) still
  # identifies whose visit this is until that happens.
  defp property_attrs(%Client{} = client) do
    %{client_id: client.id, service_address: "#{client.name} — address to be confirmed"}
  end

  defp schedule_visit(scope, %Lead{frequency: :one_time} = lead, property) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
             property_id: property.id,
             scheduled_date: lead.scheduled_date,
             start_time: lead.start_time,
             end_time: lead.end_time,
             agreed_price_cents: lead.total_cents,
             status: :scheduled
           }) do
      {:ok, %{job_id: job.id, recurring_plan_id: nil}}
    end
  end

  defp schedule_visit(scope, %Lead{} = lead, property) do
    with {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} <-
           Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(scope, %{
             property_id: property.id,
             recurrence: lead.frequency,
             start_date: lead.scheduled_date,
             occurrence_count: @default_occurrence_count,
             start_time: lead.start_time,
             end_time: lead.end_time,
             agreed_price_cents: lead.total_cents
           }) do
      {:ok, %{job_id: nil, recurring_plan_id: plan.id}}
    end
  end

  defp finalize_conversion(%Lead{} = lead, %Client{} = client, property, visit_ids) do
    lead
    |> Lead.changeset(
      Map.merge(%{status: :converted, client_id: client.id, property_id: property.id}, visit_ids)
    )
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp issue_portal_access(%Lead{} = lead, %Client{} = client) do
    with {:ok, session} <- Portal.create_portal_session(client, %{}) do
      Notifier.deliver_confirmation(lead, portal_url(session))
    end
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp portal_url(session), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/portal/access/#{session.token}"

  defp scope_for(%Lead{account_id: account_id}), do: %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole do
  @moduledoc """
  Restricts office-only surfaces — scheduling, timesheets (including
  the payroll CSV export), quality, invoices, clients, quotes,
  reminders, and the audit trail — to account owners and admins.

  A cleaner (or anyone with no office role on the active account) is
  redirected to `/field`, their own surface, with an error flash.

  ## Usage

  As a LiveView `on_mount` hook, listed after
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth`'s `:require_authenticated` in the same
  `live_session` (it relies on `current_scope.user` already being
  assigned):

      live_session :require_office_role,
        on_mount: [
          {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
          {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
        ] do
        live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
        ...
      end

  As a plug, listed after `:require_authenticated_user` in the
  pipeline, for controller routes such as the timesheet CSV export:

      pipeline :require_office_role do
        plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts

  @behaviour Plug

  @impl Plug

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story835.Criterion7112Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7112 — Owner builds a per-room quote: selecting the per-room
  pricing model and entering room counts prices the quote per room, and
  no square-footage or hourly inputs are ever requested alongside it.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  setup context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}
  end

  spex "owner builds a per-room quote" do
    scenario "the quote is priced per room with no square-footage or hourly inputs requested" do
      given_ "the owner is creating a new quote for a lead", context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the owner selects the per-room pricing model and adds 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms",
            context do
        html =
          context.quote_live
          |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
            quote: %{pricing_model: "per_room", bedroom_count: 3, bathroom_count: 2}
          )
          |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the quote is priced per room and no square-footage or hourly inputs are requested",
            context do
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='room-bedroom-count-input']")
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='room-bathroom-count-input']")
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='square-feet-input']")
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='hours-input']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

## No owner UI to manage the instant-quote rate card (booking rates only settable via console) (ID: 29ca9136-9779-4fee-8604-42e412b9f8b6)

**Severity:** high | **Scope:** app | **Status:** accepted | **Story:** 848

The public /book calculator prices from Quoting's booking rate card (per-room/sqft bases, frequency discounts, add-on prices), but no owner surface manages those fields — QA had to seed them via psql. Owners can't configure their own instant-quote pricing, which makes the public funnel unusable in practice. Needs an owner-side rate-card management UI (e.g. under /quotes or a /settings/booking page) covering base rates, frequency discounts, and add-ons.

## /book header nav overflows viewport on mobile (390px), causing horizontal scroll (ID: 8d36bfcf-006d-439b-9168-0fa8988d40a2)

**Severity:** medium | **Scope:** app | **Status:** accepted | **Story:** 848

On the public instant-quote page (/book) at a 390x844 mobile viewport, the shared root layout header's nav (Register/Log in top row, then logo + Website/GitHub/theme-toggle/Get Started second row) does not wrap or collapse. `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` measures 521px against a `clientWidth` of 390px — a 131px horizontal overflow — forcing the whole page to horizontal-scroll on mobile.

Confirmed via browser_evaluate on the live page:
```
scrollWidth: 521, clientWidth: 390
headerRect: {x:0, y:49, width:390, height:64}
innerUlRect (Website/GitHub/theme-toggle/Get Started): {x:64, width:456.97, right:521}
```

Screenshot: ~/Pictures/Vibium/07_mobile_390x844.png and 08_mobile_header_check.png (also visually shows the logo's "v1.8.9" badge crowding the "Website" link).

This is the shared `CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts.app` header (lib/cleaner_crm_web/components/layouts.ex), so it affects every page using this layout, but it's especially relevant for /book since that's the new public, mobile-first conversion funnel entry point (story 848) — a horizontally-scrolling header undermines the "one sitting" instant-quote experience on phones, the primary device for this flow.

Expected: header nav collapses into a hamburger/menu or wraps at narrow widths so the page has no horizontal overflow.
Actual: nav overflows the viewport by 131px, causing horizontal scroll.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story835.Criterion7122Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 835 — Build quotes with per-room, per-sqft, or hourly pricing
  Criterion 7122 — Rate-card change does not alter an already-sent
  quote: a sent quote captures the rates and amounts at the moment it
  was sent, so later rate-card edits never change it.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  setup context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})
    conn = CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

    {:ok, conn: conn, user: user, account: account}
  end

  spex "rate-card change does not alter an already-sent quote" do
    scenario "the previously sent quote still shows its original total after rates rise" do
      given_ "the owner sent a quote totaling $200 using the current rate card", context do
        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='rate-card-form']", rate_card: %{per_sqft_rate_cents: 10})
        |> render_submit()

        quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']",
          quote: %{client_name: "Morgan Ruiz", pricing_model: "per_sqft", square_feet: 2000}
        )
        |> render_change()

        quote_live
        |> element("[data-test='send-quote-button']")
        |> render_click()

        sent_quote_path = assert_patch(quote_live)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{quote_live: quote_live, sent_quote_path: sent_quote_path})}
      end

      when_ "the owner later raises the rate card rates", context do
        {:ok, new_quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/quotes/new")

        new_quote_live
        |> form("[data-test='rate-card-form']", rate_card: %{per_sqft_rate_cents: 20})
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the previously sent quote still shows $200 and its line items are unchanged",
            context do
        {:ok, sent_live, html} = live(context.conn, context.sent_quote_path)

        assert html =~ "$200.00"
        assert has_element?(sent_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$200.00")
        refute has_element?(sent_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$400.00")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.TemplatesTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 35ce3856: `CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistTemplate` had no
  UI to create one and no wiring to a job's checklist, so proof-of-work
  was unreachable through the live product without seeded data. No
  spex/BDD story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  setup %{conn: conn} do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    client = ClientsFixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Riverside Bungalow"})
    property = ClientsFixtures.property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "1 Main St"})

    conn = log_in_user(conn, user)

    %{conn: conn, scope: scope, client: client, property: property}
  end

  test "create_checklist_template supports sort/drop params and a blank property_id",
       %{scope: scope, property: property} do
    {:ok, template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        "name" => "Standard Clean",
        "property_id" => "",
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},
          "1" => %{"room" => "Bathroom", "task" => "Sanitize", "required" => "false"}
        }
      })

    assert template.property_id == nil
    assert length(template.items) == 2

    {:ok, updated} =
      Quality.update_checklist_template(scope, template, %{
        "property_id" => property.id,
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},
          "1" => %{"room" => "Bathroom", "task" => "Sanitize", "required" => "false"}
        },
        "items_drop" => ["1"]
      })

    assert updated.property_id == property.id
    assert length(updated.items) == 1
    assert hd(updated.items).task == "Wipe counters"
  end

  test "an empty-items create_checklist picks up the job's property template",
       %{scope: scope, client: client, property: property} do
    {:ok, _template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        "name" => "Standard Clean",
        "property_id" => property.id,
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},
          "1" => %{"room" => "Bathroom", "task" => "Sanitize", "required" => "false"}
        }
      })

    job =
      SchedulingFixtures.job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        client_id: client.id,
        status: :in_progress
      })

    {:ok, checklist} = Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [])

    assert length(checklist.items) == 2
    assert Enum.sort(Enum.map(checklist.items, & &1.task)) == ["Sanitize", "Wipe counters"]
    assert checklist.checklist_template_id != nil
  end

  test "new form saves a template", %{conn: conn, property: property} do
    {:ok, _index_live, html} = live(conn, ~p"/quality/templates")
    assert html =~ "No checklist templates yet."

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/quality/templates/new")

    submit_result =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='checklist-template-form']",
        template: %{"name" => "Standard Clean", "property_id" => property.id}
      )
      |> render_submit()

    {:ok, _index_live2, html2} = follow_redirect(submit_result, conn, ~p"/quality/templates")
    assert html2 =~ "Standard Clean"
    assert html2 =~ property.service_address
  end

  test "Add Task control appends a blank row and it can be filled in and saved", %{
    conn: conn,
    scope: scope,
    property: property
  } do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/quality/templates/new")

    refute has_element?(new_live, "[data-test='template-item-0']")

    # The "Add Task" control is a native checkbox (see
    # `TemplateFormComponent`), so checking it fires a real "change"
    # event through the existing `phx-change="validate"` binding —
    # no synthetic JS runtime needed to exercise this in LiveViewTest.
    new_live
    |> form("[data-test='checklist-template-form']", template: %{"items_sort" => ["new"]})
    |> render_change()

    assert has_element?(new_live, "[data-test='template-item-0']")

    submit_result =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='checklist-template-form']",
        template: %{
          "name" => "Standard Clean",
          "property_id" => property.id,
          "items" => %{
            "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"}
          }
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

    {:ok, _index_live2, _html2} = follow_redirect(submit_result, conn, ~p"/quality/templates")

    [template] = Quality.list_checklist_templates(scope)
    assert length(template.items) == 1
    assert hd(template.items).task == "Wipe counters"
  end

  test "edit form renders a template's persisted rows and removes one on save", %{
    conn: conn,
    scope: scope,
    property: property
  } do
    {:ok, template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        "name" => "Standard Clean",
        "property_id" => property.id,
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},
          "1" => %{"room" => "Bathroom", "task" => "Sanitize", "required" => "false"}
        }
      })

    {:ok, edit_live, edit_html} = live(conn, ~p"/quality/templates/#{template.id}/edit")
    assert edit_html =~ "Wipe counters"
    assert edit_html =~ "Sanitize"
    assert has_element?(edit_live, "[data-test='template-item-0']")
    assert has_element?(edit_live, "[data-test='template-item-1']")

    edit_submit_result =
      edit_live
      |> form("[data-test='checklist-template-form']", template: %{"items_drop" => ["1"]})
      |> render_submit()

    {:ok, _index_live, _html} = follow_redirect(edit_submit_result, conn, ~p"/quality/templates")

    reloaded = Quality.get_checklist_template!(scope, template.id)

    assert length(reloaded.items) == 1
    assert hd(reloaded.items).task == "Wipe counters"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end

  # Reviews (story 853): the public token-link review page needs no
  # login — mirrors `/invitations/accept/:token`'s `:current_user`
  # live_session so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout —
  # while the owner's review inbox is office-only, gated the same way
  # as the other office surfaces above.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :reviews_public,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/reviews/:token", ReviewLive.Public, :show
    end
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :reviews_office,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/reviews", ReviewLive.Index, :index
    end
  end

  # Portal (client magic-link) — no user auth. `/portal/access/:token`
  # exchanges a mailed/booking-issued token for a portal session
  # (plain `:browser`, like the reminder confirm/reschedule links
  # above, so `fetch_session`/`fetch_current_scope_for_user` still
  # run); every other portal route sits behind
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth`'s own session check instead.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    get "/portal/access/:token", PortalController, :access

    live_session :portal,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
      live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      live "/portal/visits/:id", PortalLive.Visit, :show
      live "/portal/invoices", PortalLive.Invoices, :index
    end
  end

  # Public booking funnel (stories 848/849) — no user auth, plain
  # `:browser` (like the reminder/reviews/portal public routes above)
  # so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout. Both routes
  # share one view module, `BookingLive.Quote` — see its moduledoc for
  # why `BookingLive.Accept` isn't routed on its own.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :public_booking,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/book", BookingLive.Quote, :new
      live "/book/accept/:token", BookingLive.Quote, :accept
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb do
  @moduledoc """
  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such
  as controllers, components, channels, and so on.

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,
  component, etc, so keep them short and clean, focused
  on imports, uses and aliases.

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions
  below. Instead, define additional modules and import
  those modules here.
  """

  use Boundary, deps: [CleanerCrm], exports: :all

  def static_paths, do: ~w(assets fonts images favicon.ico robots.txt)

  def router do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Router, helpers: false

      # Import common connection and controller functions to use in pipelines
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.Controller
      import Phoenix.LiveView.Router
    end
  end

  def channel do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Channel
    end
  end

  def controller do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Controller, formats: [:html, :json]

      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      import Plug.Conn

      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def live_view do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveView

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def live_component do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveComponent

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def html do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Component

      # Import convenience functions from controllers
      import Phoenix.Controller,
        only: [get_csrf_token: 0, view_module: 1, view_template: 1]

      # Include general helpers for rendering HTML
      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  defp html_helpers do
    quote do
      # Translation
      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      # HTML escaping functionality
      import Phoenix.HTML
      # Core UI components
      import CleanerCrmWeb.CoreComponents

      # Common modules used in templates
      alias Phoenix.LiveView.JS
      alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

      # Routes generation with the ~p sigil
      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def verified_routes do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.VerifiedRoutes,
        endpoint: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
        router: CleanerCrmWeb.Router,
        statics: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths()
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc.
  """
  defmacro __using__(which) when is_atom(which) do
    apply(__MODULE__, which, [])
  end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb do
  @moduledoc """
  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such
  as controllers, components, channels, and so on.

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,
  component, etc, so keep them short and clean, focused
  on imports, uses and aliases.

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions
  below. Instead, define additional modules and import
  those modules here.
  """

  use Boundary, deps: [CleanerCrm], exports: :all

  def static_paths, do: ~w(assets fonts images favicon.ico robots.txt)

  def router do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Router, helpers: false

      # Import common connection and controller functions to use in pipelines
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.Controller
      import Phoenix.LiveView.Router
    end
  end

  def channel do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Channel
    end
  end

  def controller do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Controller, formats: [:html, :json]

      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      import Plug.Conn

      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def live_view do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveView

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def live_component do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveComponent

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def html do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Component

      # Import convenience functions from controllers
      import Phoenix.Controller,
        only: [get_csrf_token: 0, view_module: 1, view_template: 1]

      # Include general helpers for rendering HTML
      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  defp html_helpers do
    quote do
      # Translation
      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      # HTML escaping functionality
      import Phoenix.HTML
      # Core UI components
      import CleanerCrmWeb.CoreComponents

      # Common modules used in templates
      alias Phoenix.LiveView.JS
      alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

      # Routes generation with the ~p sigil
      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def verified_routes do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.VerifiedRoutes,
        endpoint: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
        router: CleanerCrmWeb.Router,
        statics: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths()
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc.
  """
  defmacro __using__(which) when is_atom(which) do
    apply(__MODULE__, which, [])
  end
end
