defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent

  # Hosts the component in isolation (no router route required), same
  # pattern as ClientLive.PropertyFormComponentTest. Forwards the
  # component's parent notification to the test process so assertions
  # can use `assert_receive`.
  defmodule Host do
    use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

    @impl true
    def mount(_params, session, socket) do
      {:ok,
       assign(socket, %{
         test_pid: session["test_pid"],
         current_scope: session["scope"],
         action: session["action"],
         job: session["job"]
       })}
    end

    @impl true
    def render(assigns) do
      ~H"""
      <.live_component
        module={JobFormComponent}
        id="job-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@action}
        job={@job}
      />
      """
    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({JobFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  describe "creating a job" do
    test "renders the job form with the account's properties" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      assert html =~ "12 Oak Lane"
      assert html =~ "job-form"
    end

    test "creates an unassigned job and navigates to its show page" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "09:00",
            end_time: "11:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.property_id == property.id
      assert job.cleaner_id == nil
      assert job.start_time == ~T[09:00:00]
    end

    test "creates a job pre-assigned to a cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "10:00",
            end_time: "12:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "creates a job with hourly pay for the assigned cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']", job: %{pay_type: "hourly"})
      |> render_change()

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "09:00",
            end_time: "11:00",
            pay_type: "hourly",
            hourly_rate: "25.00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.pay_type == :hourly
      assert job.hourly_rate_cents == 2500
      assert job.piece_rate_cents == nil
    end

    test "creates a job with piece-rate pay" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']", job: %{pay_type: "piece_rate"})
      |> render_change()

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "09:00",
            end_time: "11:00",
            pay_type: "piece_rate",
            piece_rate: "80.00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.pay_type == :piece_rate
      assert job.piece_rate_cents == 8000
      assert job.hourly_rate_cents == nil
    end

    test "rejects a submission missing the required date" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{property_id: property.id, date: "", start_time: "09:00", end_time: "11:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='job-form']")
      assert html =~ "can't be blank" or html =~ "is required"
    end
  end

  describe "assigning a cleaner to an existing job" do
    test "renders the assignment form" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      job = job_fixture(scope, property)

      {:ok, _lv, html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      assert html =~ "assignment-form"
    end

    test "assigns the cleaner when there is no conflict" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: next_tuesday(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, %Job{} = updated}}
      assert updated.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when the cleaner has a time-off block that day" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      friday = next_friday()

      availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, %{date: friday, all_day: true})

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: friday,
          start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "conflict"
      assert html =~ "unavailable"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when it overlaps another booking for that cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      booking_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)

      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: booking_date,
        start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
      })

      second_job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: booking_date,
          start_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[13:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => second_job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "overlap"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end
  end

  describe "editing an existing job" do
    test "sets pay type and rate on a job that had none" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      job = job_fixture(scope, property)

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :edit, "job" => job})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']", job: %{pay_type: "hourly"})
      |> render_change()

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
        job: %{
          date: Date.to_iso8601(job.scheduled_date),
          start_time: "09:00",
          end_time: "11:00",
          pay_type: "hourly",
          hourly_rate: "20.00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:job_updated, %Job{} = updated}}
      assert updated.pay_type == :hourly
      assert updated.hourly_rate_cents == 2000
    end

    # Story 843 (issue ca2cb170): rescheduling only via the board's
    # inline start-time input notified the assigned cleaner
    # (`ScheduleLive.Index`'s `reschedule_job` handler); saving the
    # same reschedule through the "Edit Job" dialog silently skipped
    # it. Both paths must land the same schedule-change notification.
    test "notifies the assigned cleaner when the edit dialog reschedules the job" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          scheduled_date: next_tuesday(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :edit, "job" => job})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
        job: %{
          date: Date.to_iso8601(job.scheduled_date),
          start_time: "13:00",
          end_time: "15:00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:job_updated, %Job{} = updated}}
      assert updated.start_time == ~T[13:00:00]

      assert [notification] = schedule_change_notifications(scope, job.id)
      assert notification.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
      assert notification.status == :pending
      assert notification.change_summary =~ "9:00 AM"
      assert notification.change_summary =~ "1:00 PM"
    end

    test "does not notify the cleaner when only the price changes" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          scheduled_date: next_tuesday(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :edit, "job" => job})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
        job: %{
          date: Date.to_iso8601(job.scheduled_date),
          start_time: "09:00",
          end_time: "11:00",
          agreed_price: "150.00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

  defp schedule_change_notifications(scope, job_id) do

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.RateCardTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 29ca9136: the public `/book` instant-quote calculator
  prices from `CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard`'s base rates, frequency
  discounts, and add-on prices, but no owner UI ever set the discount
  or add-on fields (QA had to seed them via psql). No spex/BDD story
  owns this surface (story 835's own spex covers the narrower,
  cents-denominated rate-card form embedded in `QuoteLive.Builder`),
  so it's covered here instead.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow

Both accepted QA issues for story 848 are fixed, tested, and marked resolved.

**Issue 1 (no owner rate-card UI):** Added `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/quote_live/rate_card.ex`, a new office-role-gated LiveView at `/quotes/rate-card`, linked from the Quotes index page. The pre-existing cents-only mini rate-card form inside `QuoteLive.Builder` was left alone since story 835's own spex tests drive it.

**Issue 2 (mobile header overflow at 390px):** Fixed `lib/cleaner_crm_web/components/layouts.ex` — the Website/GitHub/Get Started links now collapse into a hamburger dropdown below the `sm` breakpoint, and the version badge hides on mobile, eliminating the 131px horizontal overflow without any JS changes.

Verification: clean `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, story 848 and 835 spex suites green, full test suite at 243 tests with 0 failures, and `mix format` clean. This needs a release rebuild to reach the running deployment.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead do
  @moduledoc """
  A public instant-quote submission (story 848/849): the property
  inputs and frequency/add-ons it was priced from, the price snapshot
  frozen at the moment contact info was captured, the client's contact
  details, and everything the acceptance flow (slot, cancellation-policy
  agreement, card) adds on top of it.

  ## Status

  `:quoted` — never actually persisted today (the calculator on `/book`
  prices a lead purely in memory, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.change_lead/2`)
  but kept as the schema default for a row that, in principle, exists
  before contact info locks it in.

  `:accepted` -> `:payment_pending` -> `:converted`, or `:payment_pending`
  -> `:payment_declined` (from which the client can retry). Only a
  Stripe webhook (`CleanerCrm.Booking.receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever
  moves a lead into `:converted` or `:payment_declined` — submitting
  the card just moves it to `:payment_pending`, per the same
  webhook-confirms-everything rule `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for
  invoice payments.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type pricing_model :: :per_room | :per_sqft | :hourly
  @type frequency :: :one_time | :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly
  @type status :: :quoted | :accepted | :payment_pending | :payment_declined | :converted

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          pricing_model: pricing_model() | nil,
          bedroom_count: integer() | nil,
          bathroom_count: integer() | nil,
          square_feet: integer() | nil,
          hours: integer() | nil,
          frequency: frequency(),
          add_ons: [String.t()],
          total_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          client_name: String.t() | nil,
          client_email: String.t() | nil,
          client_phone: String.t() | nil,
          acceptance_token: String.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          policy_agreed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          policy_agreed: boolean() | nil,
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "leads" do
    field :pricing_model, Ecto.Enum, values: [:per_room, :per_sqft, :hourly]
    field :bedroom_count, :integer
    field :bathroom_count, :integer
    field :square_feet, :integer
    field :hours, :integer

    field :frequency, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:one_time, :weekly, :biweekly, :monthly],
      default: :one_time

    field :add_ons, {:array, :string}, default: []
    field :total_cents, :integer

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:quoted, :accepted, :payment_pending, :payment_declined, :converted],
      default: :quoted

    field :client_name, :string
    field :client_email, :string
    field :client_phone, :string

    field :acceptance_token, :string

    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time
    field :policy_agreed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    # Not persisted as a boolean column — `confirm_booking/2` turns a
    # truthy submission into `policy_agreed_at` instead. Only exists so
    # the confirmation form has a real changeset field to bind its
    # agreement checkbox to.
    field :policy_agreed, :boolean, virtual: true, default: false

    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @quote_fields ~w(pricing_model bedroom_count bathroom_count square_feet hours frequency add_ons)a

  @doc """
  The calculator's own changeset — every pricing input, none of it
  required, so `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing` can price a live preview
  (via `Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes/1`) after every keystroke
  regardless of whether the changeset is complete yet.
  """
  def quote_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> cast(normalize_add_ons(attrs), @quote_fields)
    |> validate_number(:bedroom_count, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:bathroom_count, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:square_feet, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:hours, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
  end

  @doc """
  The full changeset used once a lead is actually persisted: the
  calculator's inputs plus the price snapshot, contact details, and
  every field the acceptance flow fills in afterward.
  """
  def changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> quote_changeset(attrs)
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :total_cents,
      :status,
      :client_name,
      :client_email,
      :client_phone,
      :acceptance_token,
      :scheduled_date,
      :start_time,
      :end_time,
      :policy_agreed_at,
      :stripe_payment_intent_id,
      :client_id,
      :property_id,
      :job_id,
      :recurring_plan_id
    ])
    |> validate_required([:client_name, :client_email, :client_phone], message: "is required")
    |> validate_number(:total_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:acceptance_token)
  end

  @doc "The slot-selection step's own changeset — just the chosen date and start time."
  def slot_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> cast(attrs, [:scheduled_date, :start_time])
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time], message: "is required")
  end

  @doc "The confirmation step's own changeset — the policy-agreement checkbox."
  def confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    cast(lead, attrs, [:policy_agreed])
  end

  # A hidden fallback input keeps `quote[add_ons][]` present in the
  # form even with every add-on unchecked (so unchecking the last one
  # actually clears it) at the cost of always submitting one blank
  # entry alongside any real ones — dropped here rather than left for
  # every caller to filter.
  defp normalize_add_ons(%{"add_ons" => list} = attrs) when is_list(list),
    do: %{attrs | "add_ons" => Enum.reject(list, &(&1 in [nil, ""]))}

  defp normalize_add_ons(attrs), do: attrs
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story849.Criterion7235Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 849 — Accept a quote and book online with card on file
  Criterion 7235 — Card is authorized for the exact quoted amount:
  the gateway authorizes exactly the quoted price, in integer cents,
  with no added fee.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the card is authorized for exactly the quoted total" do
    scenario "card is authorized for the exact quoted amount" do
      given_ "the client saw an instant quote total of $195 in integer cents", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead = Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{total_cents: 19_500})

        {:ok, accept_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        assert html =~ "$195.00"

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{lead: lead, accept_live: accept_live})}
      end

      when_ "the client completes booking with a valid card", context do
        context.accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
          booking: %{scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10), start_time: "09:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        context.accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='confirmation-form']",
          booking: %{policy_agreed: "true", payment_method: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        payload = %{
          "type" => "payment_intent.succeeded",
          "data" => %{
            "object" => %{
              "id" => "pi_test_booking_exact_amount",
              "metadata" => %{"lead_id" => to_string(context.lead.id)}
            }
          }
        }

        Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
        |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("content-type", "application/json")
        |> post("/webhooks/stripe", payload)
        |> Phoenix.ConnTest.json_response(200)

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the gateway authorizes exactly $195 with no added fee", context do
        {:ok, accept_live, html} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{context.lead.acceptance_token}")

        assert html =~ "$195.00"
        refute has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='added-fee']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

@doc """
  The slot-selection step's own changeset — the chosen date and start
  time, required and rejected outright if already in the past (issue
  4e985412: this form accepted any date, including years-old ones,
  with zero validation). `now` defaults to the real clock but takes an
  override so callers can test the boundary without sleeping.
  """
  def slot_changeset(lead, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    lead
    |> cast(attrs, [:scheduled_date, :start_time])
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time], message: "is required")
    |> validate_slot_in_future(now)
  end

  @doc "The confirmation step's own changeset — the policy-agreement checkbox."
  def confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    cast(lead, attrs, [:policy_agreed])
  end

  @doc """
  Whether a lead's `scheduled_date`/`start_time` are still ahead of
  `now` (defaulting to the real clock) — today counts only if
  `start_time` hasn't passed yet. `false` for either field unset.

  The single source of truth behind two checks: `slot_changeset/3`'s
  own validation above (the form-level guard), and
  `CleanerCrm.Booking.confirm_booking/3`'s defense-in-depth re-check
  right before a card is charged — a slot picked as "later today" can
  go stale by the time the client actually submits payment, the same
  reason `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.slot_available?/4` gets re-checked
  there too.
  """
  @spec slot_in_future?(t(), DateTime.t()) :: boolean()
  def slot_in_future?(lead, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())

  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: nil}, _now), do: false
  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{start_time: nil}, _now), do: false

  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: date, start_time: start_time}, now) do
    case Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) do
      :gt -> true
      :lt -> false
      :eq -> Time.compare(start_time, DateTime.to_time(now)) == :gt
    end
  end

  defp validate_slot_in_future(changeset, now) do
    date = get_field(changeset, :scheduled_date)
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)

    cond do
      is_nil(date) or is_nil(start_time) ->
        changeset

      slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: date, start_time: start_time}, now) ->
        changeset

      Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) == :lt ->
        add_error(changeset, :scheduled_date, "must be today or later")

      true ->
        add_error(changeset, :start_time, "must be later than the current time")
    end
  end

  time, required and rejected outright if already in the past (issue
  4e985412: this form accepted any date, including years-old ones,
  with zero validation). `now` defaults to the real clock but takes an
  override so callers can test the boundary without sleeping.
  """
  def slot_changeset(lead, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    lead
    |> cast(attrs, [:scheduled_date, :start_time])
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time], message: "is required")
    |> validate_slot_in_future(now)
  end

  @doc "The confirmation step's own changeset — the policy-agreement checkbox."
  def confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    cast(lead, attrs, [:policy_agreed])
  end

  @doc """
  Whether a lead's `scheduled_date`/`start_time` are still ahead of
  `now` (defaulting to the real clock) — today counts only if
  `start_time` hasn't passed yet. `false` for either field unset.

  The single source of truth behind two checks: `slot_changeset/3`'s
  own validation above (the form-level guard), and
  `CleanerCrm.Booking.confirm_booking/3`'s defense-in-depth re-check
  right before a card is charged — a slot picked as "later today" can
  go stale by the time the client actually submits payment, the same
  reason `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.slot_available?/4` gets re-checked
  there too.
  """
  @spec slot_in_future?(t(), DateTime.t()) :: boolean()
  def slot_in_future?(lead, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())

  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: nil}, _now), do: false
  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{start_time: nil}, _now), do: false

  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: date, start_time: start_time}, now) do
    case Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) do
      :gt -> true
      :lt -> false
      :eq -> Time.compare(start_time, DateTime.to_time(now)) == :gt
    end
  end

  defp validate_slot_in_future(changeset, now) do
    date = get_field(changeset, :scheduled_date)
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)

    cond do
      is_nil(date) or is_nil(start_time) ->
        changeset

      slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: date, start_time: start_time}, now) ->
        changeset

      Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) == :lt ->
        add_error(changeset, :scheduled_date, "must be today or later")

      true ->
        add_error(changeset, :start_time, "must be later than the current time")
    end
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead do
  @moduledoc """
  A public instant-quote submission (story 848/849): the property
  inputs and frequency/add-ons it was priced from, the price snapshot
  frozen at the moment contact info was captured, the client's contact
  details, and everything the acceptance flow (slot, cancellation-policy
  agreement, card) adds on top of it.

  ## Status

  `:quoted` — never actually persisted today (the calculator on `/book`
  prices a lead purely in memory, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.change_lead/2`)
  but kept as the schema default for a row that, in principle, exists
  before contact info locks it in.

  `:accepted` -> `:payment_pending` -> `:converted`, or `:payment_pending`
  -> `:payment_declined` (from which the client can retry). Only a
  Stripe webhook (`CleanerCrm.Booking.receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever
  moves a lead into `:converted` or `:payment_declined` — submitting
  the card just moves it to `:payment_pending`, per the same
  webhook-confirms-everything rule `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for
  invoice payments.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type pricing_model :: :per_room | :per_sqft | :hourly
  @type frequency :: :one_time | :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly
  @type status :: :quoted | :accepted | :payment_pending | :payment_declined | :converted

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          pricing_model: pricing_model() | nil,
          bedroom_count: integer() | nil,
          bathroom_count: integer() | nil,
          square_feet: integer() | nil,
          hours: integer() | nil,
          frequency: frequency(),
          add_ons: [String.t()],
          total_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          client_name: String.t() | nil,
          client_email: String.t() | nil,
          client_phone: String.t() | nil,
          acceptance_token: String.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          policy_agreed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          policy_agreed: boolean() | nil,
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "leads" do
    field :pricing_model, Ecto.Enum, values: [:per_room, :per_sqft, :hourly]
    field :bedroom_count, :integer
    field :bathroom_count, :integer
    field :square_feet, :integer
    field :hours, :integer

    field :frequency, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:one_time, :weekly, :biweekly, :monthly],
      default: :one_time

    field :add_ons, {:array, :string}, default: []
    field :total_cents, :integer

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:quoted, :accepted, :payment_pending, :payment_declined, :converted],
      default: :quoted

    field :client_name, :string
    field :client_email, :string
    field :client_phone, :string

    field :acceptance_token, :string

    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time
    field :policy_agreed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    # Not persisted as a boolean column — `confirm_booking/2` turns a
    # truthy submission into `policy_agreed_at` instead. Only exists so
    # the confirmation form has a real changeset field to bind its
    # agreement checkbox to.
    field :policy_agreed, :boolean, virtual: true, default: false

    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @quote_fields ~w(pricing_model bedroom_count bathroom_count square_feet hours frequency add_ons)a

  @doc """
  The calculator's own changeset — every pricing input, none of it
  required, so `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing` can price a live preview
  (via `Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes/1`) after every keystroke
  regardless of whether the changeset is complete yet.
  """
  def quote_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> cast(normalize_add_ons(attrs), @quote_fields)
    |> validate_number(:bedroom_count, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:bathroom_count, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:square_feet, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:hours, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
  end

  @doc """
  The full changeset used once a lead is actually persisted: the
  calculator's inputs plus the price snapshot, contact details, and
  every field the acceptance flow fills in afterward.
  """
  def changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> quote_changeset(attrs)
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :total_cents,
      :status,
      :client_name,
      :client_email,
      :client_phone,
      :acceptance_token,
      :scheduled_date,
      :start_time,
      :end_time,
      :policy_agreed_at,
      :stripe_payment_intent_id,
      :client_id,
      :property_id,
      :job_id,
      :recurring_plan_id
    ])
    |> validate_required([:client_name, :client_email, :client_phone], message: "is required")
    |> validate_number(:total_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:acceptance_token)
  end

  @doc "The slot-selection step's own changeset — just the chosen date and start time."
  def slot_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> cast(attrs, [:scheduled_date, :start_time])
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time], message: "is required")
  end

  @doc "The confirmation step's own changeset — the policy-agreement checkbox."
  def confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    cast(lead, attrs, [:policy_agreed])
  end

  # A hidden fallback input keeps `quote[add_ons][]` present in the
  # form even with every add-on unchecked (so unchecking the last one
  # actually clears it) at the cost of always submitting one blank
  # entry alongside any real ones — dropped here rather than left for
  # every caller to filter.
  defp normalize_add_ons(%{"add_ons" => list} = attrs) when is_list(list),
    do: %{attrs | "add_ons" => Enum.reject(list, &(&1 in [nil, ""]))}

  defp normalize_add_ons(attrs), do: attrs
end

      {:error, :policy_required} ->
        {:noreply, socket |> assign(:policy_required, true) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false)}

        {:noreply, socket |> assign(:slot_unavailable, true) |> assign(:policy_required, false)}

      # than leave them stuck retrying a confirmation that can never
      # succeed.
      {:error, :slot_in_past} ->
        {:noreply,
         socket
         |> assign(:step, :select_slot)
         |> assign(:slot_form, to_form(Booking.change_slot(socket.assigns.lead), as: :booking))
         |> assign(:policy_required, false)
         |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false)
         |> put_flash(:error, "That time has already passed — please pick another slot.")}

      {:error, _reason} ->
        {:noreply, socket |> assign(:slot_unavailable, true) |> assign(:policy_required, false)}
    end
  end

  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "confirming without agreeing to the cancellation policy is blocked" do
    scenario "booking is blocked without cancellation policy agreement" do
      given_ "the client has selected a slot and reached the confirmation step", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        lead = Fixtures.lead_fixture(scope, %{total_cents: 19_500})

        {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

        accept_live
        |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",

  def change_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.slot_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc """
  Validates and applies a slot choice to the (still unpersisted) lead.
  Nothing reaches the database here — `confirm_booking/2` is the only
  place a slot gets written, so availability is always checked again
  right before a card is ever charged, no matter how long a client
  lingers on the cancellation-policy step.
  """
  def select_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs) do
    with {:ok, %Lead{start_time: start_time} = slotted} <-
           lead |> Lead.slot_changeset(attrs) |> Ecto.Changeset.apply_action(:update) do
      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
    end
  end

  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, @default_visit_duration_seconds, :second)

@doc """
  Validates and applies a slot choice to the (still unpersisted) lead
  — rejected outright if the chosen date/time is already in the past
  (see `Lead.slot_changeset/3`). Nothing reaches the database here —
  `confirm_booking/3` is the only place a slot gets written, so
  availability (and, per issue 4e985412, whether the slot is still in
  the future) is always checked again right before a card is ever
  charged, no matter how long a client lingers on the
  cancellation-policy step. `now` defaults to the real clock but takes
  an override for tests.
  """
  def select_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    with {:ok, %Lead{start_time: start_time} = slotted} <-
           lead |> Lead.slot_changeset(attrs, now) |> Ecto.Changeset.apply_action(:update) do
      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
    end
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.BookingTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 4e985412: `/book/accept/:token`'s slot-selection form
  accepted any date — including years in the past — with zero
  validation, and QA drove a `scheduled_date` of 2020-01-01 all the
  way through card capture into a real scheduled job. Both guards
  added for it are exercised here:

    * `Lead.slot_changeset/3` (via `Booking.select_slot/3`) — the
      form-level guard, rejecting a past date/time outright.
    * `Booking.confirm_booking/3` — the defense-in-depth re-check
      right before a card is charged, in case a slot that was future
      at selection time goes stale (or a lead's slot fields were set
      some other way) by the time the client actually submits payment.

  No spex/BDD story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead,
  mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.TemplatesTest`'s precedent for
  issue-only coverage.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      Booking.create_lead(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  describe "select_slot/3" do
    test "rejects a scheduled_date years in the past" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => "2020-01-01",
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert "must be today or later" in errors_on(changeset).scheduled_date
    end

    test "rejects today's date once the chosen start time has already passed" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      today = Date.utc_today()
      now = DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(
                 lead,
                 %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
                 now
               )

      assert "must be later than the current time" in errors_on(changeset).start_time
    end

    test "accepts a future date" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      future_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)

      assert {:ok, slotted} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(future_date),
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert slotted.scheduled_date == future_date
    end
  end

  describe "confirm_booking/3 (defense in depth against a past slot)" do
    test "refuses a lead whose slot fields are already in the past, without charging a card" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      past_lead = %{lead | scheduled_date: ~D[2020-01-01], start_time: ~T[09:00:00]}

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(past_lead, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
      assert reloaded.status == :accepted
      assert reloaded.stripe_payment_intent_id == nil
    end

    test "refuses a slot picked for later today once that time has passed by confirmation" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      today = Date.utc_today()

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(
          lead,
          %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
          DateTime.new!(today, ~T[13:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
        )

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(
                 slotted,
                 %{"policy_agreed" => "true", "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"},
                 DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
               )
    end

    test "still confirms and moves the lead to payment_pending for a genuinely future slot" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
          "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
          "start_time" => "09:00"
        })

      assert {:ok, updated} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(slotted, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      assert updated.status == :payment_pending
    end
  end
end

  """

      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      Booking.create_lead(

          bedroom_count: 3,

  end
end

content.text:
The third issue (past-date booking acceptance) is fixed and resolved. Summary of the fix:

**Bug:** `/book/accept/:token`'s slot-selection form had zero date validation — QA drove `scheduled_date=2020-01-01` all the way through card capture into a real scheduled job.

**Fix, at both layers requested:**
- Form level — `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead.slot_changeset/3` now rejects a past date ("must be today or later") or a same-day time that's already passed ("must be later than the current time"), backed by a new `Lead.slot_in_future?/2` predicate.
- Context level (defense in depth) — `Booking.confirm_booking/3` re-checks the slot is still in the future immediately before charging the card, the same spot where slot availability is already re-checked, refusing with `{:error, :slot_in_past}` if it's gone stale between selection and confirmation. The LiveView sends the client back to slot-selection with a clear flash message in that case.

Added a regression test suite: `test/cleaner_crm/booking_test.exs` (context-level, including the exact 2020-01-01 repro and a same-day-past-time case) and `test/cleaner_crm_web/live/booking_live/accept_test.exs` (LiveView-level). Full test suite now passes at 251 tests (0 failures, up from 243 across all three fixes), story 848 and 849 spex suites are green, and `mix format` is clean.

All three accepted QA issues for story 848/849 are now resolved. This bundles the rate-card management page, the responsive mobile nav fix, and this past-date booking fix — a release rebuild is needed to get all three into the running deployment.
